title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as new players enter the in-orbit servicing market and military initiatives gain traction in Europe. Meanwhile, budget allocations and technological advancements continue to shape the landscape.

themes.title: In-Orbit Servicing Takes Off
themes.body: Revolv Space's deal with Infinite Orbits marks a notable entry into the in-orbit servicing market, signaling a growing recognition of its potential. This sector could redefine how we think about satellite longevity and maintenance.

themes.title: Military Space Command Initiatives
themes.body: Germany's push for a European military space command reflects a broader trend of nations seeking to bolster their defense capabilities in space. As geopolitical tensions rise, expect more collaborative efforts among European nations.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion addition to space resilience underscores a strategic pivot towards safeguarding space assets. This funding could enhance the U.S. military's operational capabilities in an increasingly contested environment.

themes.title: Hypersonic Tests Continue to Slip
themes.body: The repeated delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests raise questions about the pace of U.S. advancements in this critical area. As rivals make strides, the pressure mounts to deliver on these ambitious programs.
